title: Compare genomic features by interval overlap

sources.locator: Default behavior; intersecting against multiple -b files; option summary
Fundamental concepts: overlapping/intersecting features; coordinate conventions

scientific_use: Find, count, or report overlaps between genomic feature sets, such as SNPs and exons, reads and genes, or calls absent from reference catalogs. Supports questions about feature membership and shared genomic bases.
tool_role_basis: The documented task applies the existing bedtools intersect command to BED/BAM/GFF/VCF inputs; no algorithm implementation is required by these examples.
inputs: Feature set A and one or more feature set B files in BED/GFF/VCF or supported BAM forms; BED uses zero-based starts and half-open interval semantics as described in overview.

Examples name reads, genes, exons, RepeatMasker, structural variants, segmental duplications, SNP calls, dbSNP, 1000 Genomes calls, LINEs and SINEs; these are input roles/examples, not identified downloadable datasets.
outputs: Overlapping shared intervals, selected full input records, counts, or A records with/without overlaps, depending on flags; stdout or redirected files.
dependencies: bedtools2 CLI; tab-delimited feature inputs; compatible coordinate systems and chromosome naming; sort inputs for -sorted mode; optional UNIX pipelines.
evidence: intersect.rst documents default shared interval output, overlap fraction/strand/split and sorted options.
example-usage.rst demonstrates reads vs genes, exon vs RepeatMasker, structural variants vs segmental duplications, SNP calls vs dbSNP and 1KG.
overview.rst defines A/B and BED/GFF/VCF coordinate conventions.
limitations: The examples use generic filenames and do not identify exact dataset releases or accessions.
Author must choose overlap semantics and resolve data versions, assembly compatibility, sort order, and deduplication of multiple overlaps.

title: Measure feature coverage and breadth
source_kind: CLI documentation and advanced workflow examples

sources.locator: Coverage of features entirely within intervals; BAM coverage on exons; strand-specific coverage

scientific_use: For each target interval, quantify how many features overlap, how many target bases have nonzero coverage, target length and covered fraction. Examples include sequence alignments over windows or exons, with strand-specific and proper-pair variants.
tool_role_basis: The source composes bedtools coverage and bamtobed with optional samtools filtering; it uses existing tools to analyze supplied alignments and intervals.
inputs: Target intervals in A and reads/alignments or other features in B; examples use exon, gene and arbitrary window BEDs with BAM reads.
outputs: Per-target overlap count, covered bases, target length and breadth fraction; optional per-position depth or histograms.
dependencies: bedtools2; optionally samtools for BAM filtering; sorted inputs and -sorted mode for memory-efficient large-file processing; genome assembly agreement.
evidence: coverage.rst describes A/B semantics, coverage outputs, -d, -hist, strand filters and memory-efficient sorted mode.
advanced-usage.rst shows bamtobed to coverage and proper-pair filtering with samtools.
limitations: No named read dataset or target annotation is supplied by the examples.
Coverage semantics depend on feature overlap criteria, alignment filtering and target intervals; user must resolve read pairing and strand requirements.

title: Summarize genome-wide feature depth

sources.locator: Default behavior; histogram and BEDGRAPH examples
bedtools genomecov section; capture coverage pipeline

scientific_use: Measure genome-wide coverage depth, including the number and fraction of bases at each depth; assess uniformity of whole-genome sequencing or find uncovered target portions by combining bedgraph output with interval overlap.
tool_role_basis: The documented examples apply genomecov to feature or BAM inputs and combine its output with standard stream filters and intersect.
inputs: Genome-sized feature intervals or BAM alignments, plus a genome file for interval input; tutorial also pipes BAM genome coverage through bedgraph and filters zero-depth regions.
outputs: Per-genome/per-chromosome depth histogram or BEDGRAPH intervals annotated with depth; downstream uncovered portions of target intervals.
dependencies: bedtools2; assembly-matched chromosome sizes; sorted feature input where required by documented example; optional awk and intersect for a chained coverage analysis.
evidence: genomecov.rst says coverage histogram supports sequencing uniformity assessment and demonstrates histogram and BEDGRAPH output.
tutorial/bedtools.md describes capture-region uncovered-base extraction using genomecov -bga and intersect.
limitations: Tutorial warns its genome-wide exons example takes about three minutes; no actual execution performed.
Genome file, assembly and choice of BAM/interval treatment must be supplied consistently.

title: Compare interval-set similarity with Jaccard statistics
source_kind: CLI documentation and scientific tutorial analysis

sources.locator: Principal component analysis; all pairwise fetal tissue comparisons

scientific_use: Quantify base-pair overlap similarity of two interval sets. The tutorial compares DNase hypersensitivity sites between same and different fetal tissue samples, then proposes all-pairs tissue similarity, matrix construction, clustering/PCA and heatmap visualization.
tool_role_basis: bedtools jaccard computes the statistic; GNU parallel, Python matrix formatting and R plotting compose existing tools around it.
inputs: Two sorted BED/GFF/VCF interval sets per comparison. Tutorial uses merged DNase hypersensitivity site sets for fetal tissue samples; example sample labels include fHeart DS16621, fHeart DS15839 and fetal skin/fibroblast sample DS19745 on hg19.
outputs: Intersection length, union-minus-intersection length, Jaccard score and intersection count; tutorial derives an all-pairs matrix and plots PCA/heatmap.
dependencies: bedtools2; sorted inputs; tutorial's pairwise workflow uses GNU parallel and shell text utilities, a referenced make-matrix.py script, and R packages ggplot2, RColorBrewer and gplots.
evidence: jaccard.rst defines base-pair intersection/union statistic and output fields.

tutorial/bedtools.md gives same-tissue versus different-tissue comparisons and all 400 pairwise comparisons among 20 fetal tissue samples; states PCA is a toy example and heatmaps are more informative for distance.
limitations: Tutorial does not provide stable accession links for the 20 merged BED files or make-matrix.py; source data availability and terms remain unknown.
Jaccard result depends on interval merge policy, genome build and any overlap fraction/strand options.
No computation or plot reproduction was run.

title: Test interval overlap enrichment with Fisher's exact test
source_kind: CLI documentation and methodological evaluation description
scientific_use: Estimate whether overlap between two interval sets exceeds expectations given estimated possible intervals and genome size; report left, right and two-tail Fisher p-values and a contingency table.
tool_role_basis: The documented command applies bedtools fisher to feature files and a genome size file; source implementation is not proposed as task work.
inputs: Two presorted BED/GFF/VCF interval sets and a genome file; documentation's miniature example has three A intervals, two B intervals and a one-chromosome genome.
outputs: Overlap counts, estimated possible interval count, contingency table, p-values and ratio.
dependencies: bedtools2 fisher; compatible genome size file; presorted input intervals.
evidence: fisher.rst worked example uses 500 and 60 base genome sizes and explains contingency table.
Evaluation section describes chromosome 1 canonical genes and 1000 shuffled interval replicates; reports inflation and recommends simulation to validate low p-values.
limitations: The possible-interval count is heuristic and p-values depend strongly on it; documentation explicitly recommends simulation validation.
The evaluation data and simulation outputs are not included in this pass; no inference about calibration beyond source text.

title: Compare relative distances between feature sets
source_kind: CLI documentation with bundled demonstration data

sources.locator: Definition and default behavior; exon-AluY and exon-GERP examples

scientific_use: Summarize relative distance from each A interval to its two closest B intervals, yielding a distribution from 0 to 0.5. Contrast exon-to-AluY and exon-to-conserved-element examples to examine spatial association beyond direct overlap.
tool_role_basis: The unit applies the documented reldist command to supplied interval datasets; it does not alter the algorithm.
inputs: Repository demonstration files data/refseq.chr1.exons.bed.gz with data/aluY.chr1.bed.gz or data/gerp.chr1.bed.gz.
outputs: Relative-distance bins with counts, total and fractions, or per-A distances with -detail.
dependencies: bedtools2; documented inputs should be compatible genomic intervals; sorted input is indicated by related documentation/tool constraints to confirm for selected version.
evidence: reldist.rst defines relative distance distribution and states uniformity as expectation without spatial correlation.
Worked examples use three named repository data files and show 43,408/43,422 total exon intervals.
limitations: The files were not downloaded or previewed; biological assembly, release, source accession, file terms and observed provenance are not specified in inspected documentation.
The documentation gives a 2012 Favorov et al. metric citation but does not establish provenance of demonstration files.

title: Find nearest genomic features to variants

sources.locator: Puzzles: average distance from GWAS SNPs to closest exon

scientific_use: Annotate query variants/features with the nearest feature, including signed/upstream distance options; tutorial asks for average distance from GWAS SNPs to closest exon.
tool_role_basis: The operation uses the existing closest command on variant and exon intervals.
inputs: A query interval file, such as GWAS SNPs, and sorted B annotation intervals, such as exons; compatible chromosome/assembly and optional strand policy.
outputs: Nearest B feature fields per A feature, optionally distance; overlaps count as closest by default.
dependencies: bedtools2 closest; presorted interval files; all files must share chromosome sort order for multiple B inputs.
evidence: closest.rst describes nearest-feature behavior and GWAS polymorphism/gene example.
tutorial/bedtools.md asks for mean GWAS SNP-to-nearest-exon distance.
limitations: Tutorial puzzle provides no actual GWAS or exon dataset location, assembly, filtering, or expected answer.
Mean-distance task needs a defined treatment for chromosome mismatches/no feature and overlapping SNPs.

title: Mask non-target genome sequence around capture intervals

sources.locator: Mask all regions in a genome except for targeted capture regions

scientific_use: Expand target probe intervals, compute their complement and use the complement as mask intervals in a reference FASTA, leaving target regions unmasked. A useful preprocessing workflow for restricting downstream analyses to capture territory.
tool_role_basis: The example composes existing bedtools slop and complement with bedtools maskfasta; it configures tools without implementing an algorithm.
inputs: Probe BED intervals, chromosome sizes genome file, and reference FASTA matching the hg18 example; 500 bp flank added to each probe.
The source example names hg18.genome; repository genomes/human.hg18.genome is a candidate chromosome-size file by filename, not confirmed as the exact asset.
outputs: Expanded probes, complement intervals, and a masked FASTA with bases outside expanded targets masked.
dependencies: bedtools2 slop/complement/maskfasta; reference FASTA and chromosome sizes for same assembly; inputs must use compatible coordinates.
evidence: advanced-usage.rst gives three command steps and names hg18.genome/hg18.fa in example.
The tree contains genomes/human.hg18.genome (868 bytes); mapping it to example hg18.genome is an inference.
limitations: Example reference FASTA and probes are placeholders and are not identified as bundled assets; exact masking character and output validation are not described in inspected section.
No execution performed; reference release, access and redistribution terms unresolved.

title: Partition genomic regions by recurrence across feature sets
scientific_use: Partition genomic intervals into subintervals and report how many input files and which files overlap each segment; supports recurrence/consensus summaries across multiple feature sets.
tool_role_basis: The operation applies the existing multiinter command to sorted interval inputs.
inputs: Two or more sorted BED interval files in the same chromosome ordering; the documentation says the command inspects intervals from each input.
outputs: Subintervals with overlap count, list of contributing file indices and per-file 0/1 overlap indicators.
dependencies: bedtools2; all interval inputs sorted in the same manner; optional genome order handling per command options.
evidence: multiinter.rst defines common intervals among multiple files and documents output for subintervals overlapped by 0 through N files.
limitations: No named biological datasets or downstream consensus threshold are supplied; the author must define how overlap recurrence maps to a scientific question.

title: Generate randomized genomic intervals for null comparisons
scientific_use: Randomly relocate a set of genomic features within a genome, optionally maintaining chromosome, excluding masked regions, avoiding interval overlap, and fixing a random seed. Supports empirical null comparisons for spatial overlap or proximity analyses.
tool_role_basis: The documented workflow uses existing shuffle outputs as randomized feature sets for downstream comparisons.
inputs: Feature intervals and a chromosome-size genome file; optional exclusion intervals and seed.
outputs: Randomized intervals preserving input feature lengths, with placement constraints controlled by options (details should be confirmed for the selected options).
dependencies: bedtools2 shuffle; genome sizes; optional exclusion BED and downstream intersect/fisher/statistic command.
evidence: shuffle.rst says it randomly permutes genomic locations and documents seed, chromosome, exclusion and non-overlap options.
fisher.rst evaluation compares its result to shuffled-data simulations.
limitations: A null model requires explicit placement assumptions; uniform-over-genome and uniform-over-chromosome options differ.
No empirical task inputs, replicate count or statistic are specified by the shuffle page alone.

title: Extract reference sequence for genomic intervals
scientific_use: Retrieve reference nucleotide sequences corresponding to genomic features, including concatenation of BED12 blocks such as exons; can support sequence extraction for downstream motif or sequence analyses.
tool_role_basis: The documented operation applies getfasta to a reference FASTA and feature intervals.
inputs: Reference FASTA plus BED/GFF/VCF intervals; BED12 block-aware extraction is documented.
outputs: FASTA records for each interval, with header choices controlled by feature names/attributes and reverse-complement options in the command interface.
dependencies: bedtools2 getfasta; reference FASTA index and compatible genome assembly; exact coordinate convention and strand behavior must be set appropriately.
evidence: getfasta.rst describes sequence extraction, FASTA output, block concatenation for BED12 and GFF3 nameKey behavior.
limitations: No concrete biological sequence dataset is linked by inspected documentation excerpt.
A source reference genome and matching annotation need release/access/terms review; extraction was not executed.

title: Aggregate values from overlapping genomic features
scientific_use: Map scores or other values from overlapping B intervals to each A feature and summarize with an operation; documentation example computes mean BEDGRAPH score over genes, and mentions counting exome alignments per exon.
tool_role_basis: The task uses the existing map command to aggregate overlapping feature values.
inputs: A feature intervals such as genes or exons; B intervals with a numeric/value column such as BEDGRAPH signal or read alignments.
outputs: A records annotated with aggregate(s) of selected B column values for overlapping intervals.
dependencies: bedtools2 map; sorted inputs by genomic coordinate; selected B column and aggregation operation.
evidence: map.rst gives genes BED plus peaks BEDGRAPH and `-c 4 -o mean` example; notes sorted-input requirement and exon alignment count example.
limitations: The external Biostars example and full option semantics were not inspected; no named dataset or biological question is supplied.

title: Construct merged genomic regions and summarize contributing features

sources.locator: Merge intervals; count overlaps; merge nearby features

scientific_use: Collapse overlapping or book-ended intervals into contiguous regions and optionally summarize contributor counts or names; the tutorial applies this to exon intervals and notes merging nearby regions by a distance threshold.
tool_role_basis: The unit applies the existing merge command to sorted feature intervals and requests summaries through its options.
inputs: Sorted BED/GFF/VCF/BAM-derived intervals; optional distance threshold and columns to summarize.
outputs: Merged intervals, optionally annotated with counts, collapsed names or other column summaries.
dependencies: bedtools2 merge; presorted input; meaningful choice of distance threshold and columns/operations.
evidence: merge.rst defines merging overlapping/book-ended features, sorting requirement, count/collapse summaries and distance option.
tutorial/bedtools.md demonstrates merged exon records and `-d 1000` proximity merging.
limitations: The tutorial's exon input is a placeholder path and not linked to a particular annotation source.
Merge distance and strand handling alter biological interpretation and must be specified.

title: Find genomic regions not covered by an annotation
scientific_use: Return genomic intervals not covered by a feature set, such as non-exonic regions or unbound portions of the genome; requires explicit chromosome lengths to delimit the complement.
tool_role_basis: The operation applies bedtools complement to existing interval annotations and a genome-size file.
inputs: BED/GFF/VCF feature intervals and assembly-matched chromosome sizes; tutorial example uses exon intervals.
outputs: Intervals spanning portions of chromosomes not covered by the input features, written as interval records.
dependencies: bedtools2 complement; genome-size file; compatible assembly and sorted inputs where required.
evidence: complement.rst defines output as intervals not covered by any input interval and shows a genome-size file requirement.
tutorial describes deriving non-exonic intervals from exons.
limitations: No biological annotation source/release is identified for the tutorial exon example.
Result depends on the genome sizes and chromosome scope chosen.

title: Construct strand-aware intervals adjacent to genomic features

sources.locator: Overview; genome boundary and strand options
Puzzles: create two-base splice-site intervals at exon sides

scientific_use: Create upstream/downstream intervals around each feature while clipping at chromosome boundaries; strand-aware left/right distances can construct intervals such as canonical splice-site windows beside exons.
tool_role_basis: The documented examples apply the flank command to feature intervals using supplied genome sizes and flank distances.
inputs: BED/GFF/VCF features, chromosome sizes, and symmetric or separate left/right lengths; optional strand-aware and proportional length controls.
outputs: Two flanking intervals around each input feature, restricted to chromosome bounds.
dependencies: bedtools2 flank; assembly-matched genome size file; strand/coordinate interpretation and chosen widths.
evidence: flank.rst says two intervals are created per feature, chromosome boundaries are enforced and genome sizes are required; -s interprets lengths by strand.
tutorial puzzle asks for 2 bp canonical splice-site intervals on both sides of each exon.
limitations: Tutorial explicitly says not to exclude splice sites at first or last exon; task author should preserve or revise that simplification explicitly.
No exon source/release is provided; splice-coordinate convention needs grading specification.

title: Find features within a genomic neighborhood
scientific_use: Find features overlapping a neighborhood around each query interval, for example genes within 10 kb of CNVs; supports symmetric/asymmetric and strand-oriented neighborhoods, and can count nearby features.
tool_role_basis: The source applies bedtools window to interval inputs; it does not implement a new algorithm.
inputs: Query intervals such as CNVs and database features such as genes in BED/GFF/VCF or BAM forms; optional flank width or separate left/right widths.
outputs: Overlapping nearby feature pairs, original A entries with any hit, or per-A counts, depending on options.
dependencies: bedtools2 window; matching genome assembly and coordinate conventions; strand information for strand-oriented windows.
evidence: window.rst describes default 1000 bp up/downstream search and -w/-l/-r/-sw/-c controls.
example-usage.rst proposes genes within 10,000 bp upstream/downstream of CNVs.
limitations: The CNV and gene examples do not identify particular datasets, assembly, or release.
The chosen neighborhood width and whether strand should define upstream/downstream require a scientific rationale.

title: Annotate features against several genomic tracks
scientific_use: For each query feature, report fraction covered and/or number of overlapping features from multiple annotation tracks in one operation. Example annotates variants against genes, conserved intervals and known variants.
tool_role_basis: The documented operation applies bedtools annotate to variant intervals and existing annotation tracks.
inputs: Query BED/VCF/GFF features and multiple feature files such as genes, conservation intervals and known variant sites; optional strand rules.
outputs: Original query records followed by per-track coverage fractions, hit counts, or both.
dependencies: bedtools2 annotate; compatible reference assembly and coordinate conventions for every track.
evidence: annotate.rst defines coverage and overlap-count annotation across multiple tracks and supplies a variants/genes/conserve/known_var worked example with outputs.
limitations: Example intervals are toy records, not identified study datasets.
Fraction covered and feature count represent different quantities and should be selected explicitly for grading.

title: Compare alignment counts across BAM samples at target intervals
scientific_use: Count alignments from multiple BAM samples overlapping each target interval, producing comparable per-target count columns; may support sample-wise coverage comparisons at genes, exons or other regions.
tool_role_basis: The example applies bedtools multicov to a BED target file and existing indexed BAM files.
inputs: BED/GFF/VCF intervals and one or more position-sorted, indexed BAM files; optional mapping-quality, duplicate, QC, proper-pair, strand and overlap filters.
outputs: Original target interval row followed by one overlapping alignment count per BAM in command-line order.
dependencies: bedtools2 multicov; BAM index files, created after coordinate sorting with samtools or bamtools; assembly compatibility.
evidence: multicov.rst describes per-interval counts from multiple indexed BAM files and provides a three-BAM example.
limitations: Example BAM files are illustrative and do not identify a study or sample design.
Counts are not normalized and depend on filtering and mapping-quality choices; downstream comparison method is unspecified.
